summary: Rabbi Harari discusses whether oven racks require tevilat kelim, examining the definition of a utensil used for food production. He reviews several halakhic perspectives, including the importance of majority usage and whether stationary oven components qualify as utensils of the meal. The class concludes by presenting multiple reasons why oven racks generally do not require immersion.
questions: Do the racks in a kitchen oven need to be dipped?
Does the fact that I sometimes put food directly on the rack change the requirement for tevilat kelim?
Does the majority usage of a utensil determine if it needs to be immersed?
Are oven racks considered utensils of the meal if they are not moved to the table?
